questions.stem: How do insulin and glucagon work together to control blood glucose?

options.text: They both raise blood glucose levels
They both lower blood glucose levels
Insulin lowers blood glucose while glucagon raises it, acting as antagonistic hormones
They are released at the same time and have the same effect

questions.explanation: Insulin and glucagon are antagonistic hormones. Insulin lowers blood glucose by converting glucose to glycogen, while glucagon raises it by converting glycogen back to glucose. This is an example of negative feedback.
